memos.content:
It's been a good few days. Really settling into the new routines and habits and it feels very natural. Hanna even commented that we laugh a lot more these days, and we really enjoy everyday and are able to get through stressful moments no problem. Hannas mom has been coming by a couple times the last few days, and it's been good to see that overall. However, first thing she Said yesterday was negative... But Hanna called her on it immediately. And she tries to still buy toys from thrift shops for Asher which is fine except it's literally every single time she sees him and it's hard for him to understand why we can't do the same for him everywhere we go. Hanna has tried to talk to her but she has yet to really listen. The toys are usually broken and cheap. Hanna and I both believe it would be better to buy less, but higher quality toys for him. Ah well.

My mom is not reacting well to the boundaries, not that I've explained them to her or had her ask me. We've cancelled for Easter and will do our own things, which is exciting. Dad and I made plans for coffee on Friday and met, and she just decided to show up, which kinda ruined it a bit. I'm always so on edge and basically prepared for criticism and questioning whenever I'm around her and I can't stand it. Hence the new boundaries. Which both Hanna and I are excited about. 

Hannas mom is still a bit of a question mark, she's said to Hanna she sees how happy we are but we also still stress when she comes over about the house and how it could be seen by her. She hasn't opened a conversation with me at all and continues to be very cold to me. It's getting very frustrating to see how she treats Hanna and avoids spending time with her and the kids except for brief moments. She even said she's going to leave for a vacation at Christmas which Hanna found to be very hurtful. I think honestly, she is angry about how things have worked out. Maybe because the men in her life didn't do that, but that's not my problem or Hannas. I wish she would be more mature and supportive of our family overall. 

We're on a week into taking over the budget and while I'm struggling to handle the overdraft we sit in sometimes in YNAB, I am really thankful that we're in control now, and Hanna and I are working on this stuff together. I think a lot about the family, our future and the budget, and it's not overwhelming, its just nice to be really attuned as a team these days. I am going to give up most (if not all) of my spending this month, until I'm working, to try to get us out of overdraft and payback the overspending I've had the last few months, then start to attack the debt. If that means paying minimums on the cards for now, so be it.

I have an interview tomorrow at the city and that's really exciting. I would love to start working asap and start being able to get ourselves into a much better financial position, so we can save, dream and plan for things beyond the basics. Fingers crossed. 👍🏻 

I finished cleaning up Dan's and all my stuff is home, both Hanna and I are super excited and happy. I'm home. I'm here to stay. Our routines and family is stronger, healthier and frankly, happier. I am so proud of myself and the work I've put in. Feel so healthy, mind and body. I am sore, tired, and sometimes exhausted but it's all feeling really good. Purpose really does help. 

Today, made a huge breakfast like I did yesterday, dishes, laundry, garbage taken out, got gas, cleaned Dan's, swimming with Margs, and setup the bed for some fun for Hanna and I, as well as cleaned out the drawers of socks with holes for both of us. AND organized the drawers and put away clothes, as I push laundry along. I am so proud of my work.

Rest of day should be somewhat chill - laundry folding, budget updating, and continue to inventory my cards to sell one day. And find stuff to sell from our house. 🏠😎

Good days. Love this family. So thankful, for everyone and everything in my life. The people who have showed up and been there. Endlessly thankful.

Still haven't smoked or even really craved it. I've thought about it when I game sometimes but it doesn't stop me or make me need it. Just observing how it was really codependent with gaming. It's good to break that cycle.

memos.creator: users/scootr
memos.content:
A bit of a mixed day. I'm pretty full of emotions. Fear. Thankfulness. Frustration. And I'm trying to navigate them with patience and empathy. For myself. For my partner. For her family. 

We started off by waking early with Margs and I went downstairs and got breakfast made for everyone and we had a lovely morning together. Hung out and watched some movies/TV after, and we were going to go to Costco but found out it was closed. 

We also planned to go to Pan Am to swim but Asher negated that idea - we only had a 4 hour window as it was a holiday today, so we weren't able to do that. We decided to move forward with the volcano project - which was a big one - and one I was really looking Forward to doing as a family. Unfortunately - I guess my tone was seen and heard as anger and controlling, and Hanna felt she wasn't welcome to help or participate even though I hadn't said that or intended that to be the way she felt. I did however, feel a bit frustrated that she was on the phone with Heather and just not interested (it seemed to me) to want to participate in the volcano work, as it was a lot. I know sometimes I get very focused and I go into "go mode" but it was purely trying to make sure we had time to do the thing we wanted to do. Asher was so excited. 

So ultimately Hanna was upset and defensive and reacted with a lot of anger including raising her voice and no matter how many times I apologized, shared my intent, understood where she was coming from based on my previous behavior, she just kept coming at me and not really being interested in speaking about it together or focusing on understanding each other's point of view. I felt like I understood, took accountability and said I'd work on my focused tone. There was absolutely no thought or intent of doing anything BUT doing this fun project together as a family so I was pretty sad and disappointed and frankly, confused by her reaction, though I understand she is going to lean on 13 years of experience vs 3 weeks. She asked for space, and I gave her that I thought, and when she came into the kitchen to take Margs for a nap, I asked if we could talk and she said yes, so I thought she was ok with that but that actually made her think I wasn't listening to her, which again I found very confusing as I had asked her if it was ok to talk first. She asked that I no longer ask if it's ok and just let her decide when she wants to talk. After a bit she came and thanked me for the space and we really chalked it up to a misunderstanding, and that I reinforced that I was sorry, wanted to do things together and only ever think about taking cards and trying to do more for the family, there was no intent to make her feel excluded, and I apologized that my tone made her feel that way. She apologized, as she had said "I was just a guest in the house" and that she didn't have to back down and that I could go at "anytime" which I found really hurtful, and intentionally hurtful, whereas I was just trying to do a task as a family and had a poor tone. Still, I am feeling very scared and no longer confident that things are ok since she can jump to that level of anger and not be willing to talk it out or hear me at all, whereas I felt I was hearing her and being accountable and apologizing from the moment she shared she felt she wasn't welcome. It hurts to know she is so angry at me so quickly. I feel like I'm doing so much hard work on myself and it's really hard to understand how that escalated when I'm apologizing and being accountable and sharing it wasn't the intent from the beginning. Lessons. Going to try to ensure when I'm focused I soften my tone. Even if that tone is normal in my workplaces or at my families house, it isn't something Hanna wants and I want to ensure she knows I'm listening to everything she shares and wants. 

Played with Asher who is quite sick, and he was acting out quite a bit including biting me a few times, pushing his sister, hitting and kicking but we navigated it together. He didn't want to go for a walk or anything like that, so we tried to focus on new activities while we waited for the paper mache volcano to dry. I think Hanna and I did a great job building it. I was pretty happy we were able to navigate that.

Nanny wanted to come over but insisted that if she did I would have to give her space and not be about at all. Which really hurts honestly, and I find her behavior to be really childish frankly. I am being the adult in this somehow. So I suggested to Hanna, as much as it hurt, that she could come over and finish painting and doing the volcano lava part with the kids and Hanna. I want her to know I am not in the way, nor trying to do anything to harm her relationship with Hanna or the kids, despite her obvious attempts to do that to me over the past 2 months. But I forgive her. That's her issue and attitude and I'm not responsible for fixing that or addressing it. 

So I'm upstairs, folding laundry and putting things away because suddenly Hanna is stressing about the house, because of what her mom may or may not think. I really don't give a fuck, to be honest, because I'm so happy with myself and my efforts, I'm on top of everything, maybe a bit too much (as the volcano project proved). So I am getting the laundry put away and tidied up upstairs. Afraid and honestly frustrated I can't go put in laundry because she's here, and Hanna worries it'll be seen as "performative" even though if that was the case the house would be a mess, but it's actually my routine and focus. Every day. That's why the house is clean. Hanna hasn't done a lot lately and that's the intent but I'm still being judged as it I don't do anything. Really sucks. 

People. I wasn't well. I was sick. Sometimes I wish I had fucking cancer or some other ailment that people could sympathize with instead of mental health and addiction. Maybe there would be more understanding. It's not like I'm asking to be excused from what happened, I'm accountable, but I'm never going to say I had intent to hurt or act out, ever, because I didn't. I wasn't well. I didn't take care of myself. That's my accountability. But I'm being painted as if I'm just a complete piece of shit that is irredeemably broken and doesn't deserve to be around his own family. 

Feeling pretty down. Locked in a cage a bit. In what was and is my house too, but I'm not going to say that to Hanna as she has shared she has leverage to take the kids, etc. feels like I have a gun to my head and people want me to fuck up so they can point and say that's who I am, who I Always was. 

Nah. Who I am is who I am when I'm healthy. I'm capable. Responsible. Empathetic. Strong. Resilient. And I'll never stop doing the right things for myself and for our family.

It's also become pretty obvious that a lot of my issues are rooted in my mom and her own anxiety and bullshit. I'm building boundaries and not replying as much or sharing details as much because I don't trust her anymore. I actually don't want much to do with her anymore as I do blame her for some of my issues around anxiety, motivation, emotional regulation etc, and she's always been unwilling to hear what I have to say. So that's fine, boundaries will be created. And frankly with Colleen as well, until she feels mature enough to admit she had me wrong.

Tony doesn't think much of me anymore. Pretty sure that comes from Hilary. Pretty sure I lost a lot of relationships and respect from people I respect and cared about and I have to be understanding that those relationships are going to become distant if anything at all. I'm thankful for my true friends. I'm thankful for being with my family. And I'm thankful that I can move forward with Hanna, and there is understanding, even her therapist said there will be moments but that's evidence of someone working on things. It cant be perfection and perfect health immediately. Even if that's what people want or expect, even when they don't expect it of themselves or their own kids. Hurts to be judged by such a strong approach, but yet those same people don't hold themselves to the same standard.

Feeling pretty sad and alone today. Feeling like Hanna could just toss me aside at any point. Feeling like I am walking on eggshells and have a gun to my head. I just wanna be accepted for the imperfect human that I am. But one that is and always has been loving, empathetic and caring - even if I didn't take care of myself the right ways.

But I'm doing that now. That's all that matters. 

Really wish I could bring down the laundry and get it started but also don't wanna be "performative" so I'm gonna take Hannas advice and lie down up here and avoid any issues or misconception cause it seems like Colleen is eager to make that case.

We had to get going quick this morning as Hanna is going into the ER to try to get treatment for what her doctors believe is CIPD. Which is a very scary degenerative neuropathy. They said that it's a 30 hour wait but she's trying to lean on her connections and really advocate for herself which is really good for getting help as soon as we can. I've started a health log for her so we can have that. It was recommended in several "how to support" documents. 

Hanna has shared she still (understandably) has waves of anger towards me, and Ive shared that I love her, that I'll always be sorry for how I impacted her, and how I didn't take care of my health. My impacts were never intentional but it doesn't matter when the impact is the impact. I know this is going to take time to heal and rebuild trust, and I'm here to do anything to help rebuild our relationship healthier and stronger. 

She shared her frustration and anger with my parents and I'm so frustrated with them too, because of how they have been biased and honestly have contributed to me not making a change - I imagine they think they were doing their best but having them out of town was actually nice for me and Hanna. Dad hasn't been doing much in the budget chat so maybe he knows we want to pull back from it. Or he remembers how I shared that it was frustrating and anxiety producing for Hanna, and made her feel like she didn't have any control of her finances or business. I've shared and reiterated to Hanna that I'm comfortable with any plan she feels is better for her and her business, and I'll adjust and learn. On the finances front I've been doing great compared to the last few months. The dumb spending is over. 

I think boundaries need to be set with my parents. My mom's incredibly inappropriate ways of sharing information is really gross. It's always been a problem but it became amplified when shortly after separation she had informed multitudes of family, and when I told her that wasn't ok, she was defensive and minimized my concerns (gas lighting again). She asked Hanna this week first thing at her hair appointment if she could share her HEALTH ISSUES with others.... It's so inappropriate. She's such a gross gossip. I think she does it for attention. Not unlike how I've done something similar in the past and am now hyper aware of when I do that. 

Talk about working under stress, this is stressful. But I'm still on top of things. Still got things to do today.

- schedule/start claim for windshield repair
- clean bathroom 😎
- laundry - kids folded and put away and put in towels and H/J stuff.

And with these in mind I started thinking about what is on Hannas plate and how this month separation feels like it will only throw the cards back on her plate and she can hope for some support to pick up some of them. So I wrote this out to talk to her today. 

Thoughts on plan/ health

- understand how you're feeling and how it's pretty wild to see this change and believe it's sustainable. My self-care won't stop whether I'm working or not. I understand and really feel for how hard this is on you.
- one of the issues was domestic imbalance and the more I listen to fair play the more I recognize how little I was contributing and that's on me..that said, if we are to have this break, the house and domestic cards will fall back on to you primarily, while also adding additional ones like planning/packing for drops and exchanges. With you being sick and struggling the way you are, which I know you hate to admit, this seems even more unfair to you. 
- when I work I'll just get more done in the evening and lunches and breaks. Doctors appointments, gifts, event planning, errands, etc. I am confident that my brain and approach is not only sustainable, but also will improve. I want to hold half the cards, or more, right now while you are struggling with your health and mobility. We can delay the lawyer stuff until enough time and evidence has been seen by you. But I don't want you to take on more while you are alone and in the house. 
- an option would be that we swap who is in the house every few days. That way the domestic work is still being done and split. This may be a bit of a challenge initially but I believe it's very common in couples who are working together to find out if they are in the same page, and I know we are. We don't want to have our kids split between houses. We don't want to go though an expensive process of divorce. We want to dream and grow and build routines for our family that work for us. 
- I know that it's hard to Believe your are thinking for yourself but I see a strong and confident mindset from you and a willingness to be open with tough topics and feedback. And I will continue to be the guy you see now, everyday. I believe in your heart, you want support, you want to be cared for and have a lot of the cards off your plate so you can focus on self care, time to process and work on your passions. I want to allow time for that too, without leaving you to take on the majority of the domestic work when I'm gone. Your mom is busy, and I know she wants to help but she has tried to be there as much as she can and I'm simply more available and ready to do things without praise, without reminders and without you having to worry about the card carrying.

I hope you understand this primarily is coming from a place of worrying about your health, the need for rest and self care, and not adding more to your overwhelmed plate right now. You can do it I'm sure, but you don't have to. I am here, willing to take every card you want off your mind. I am here, willing to be up each night, and work each day, for this family and your dreams and ambitions. This is not a temporary mindset. This is clarity, finally. And, ultimately, it will allow us to see each other honestly, and you can witness the consistentcy and the cards disappear from your mind. 

You deserve the most support and rest you can get. You deserve a partner who is going to truly take on the cards and be a true team player. And I'm ready to go in. 

Nothing matters more to me than working, supporting and being with my family. It's clearer everyday. I appreciate you listening to this, and understand that you will need to take time to heal and evaluate and rest and recover. And I'm here, anytime, anywhere, to help you.

Back at the house this morning with Margaux. Starting around 6:15 and tough to get up this morning and it was really cold. It was really cold outside. In fact, I would say that the vehicle was fully frosted, unfortunately, but it's really nice to spend time at the house. that said. I'm really heartbroken and really sad that me and Hanna right now aren't a thing and as much as I know it's a separation. It's not a divorce yet and we have opportunities to listen and grow, but I have an opportunity to continue to be a part of their lives as well as her life. I'm just hoping that maybe we have an opportunity to go out on some dates in the future. Really sit down one-on-one and rediscover why we love each other so much because I know part of the reason that she wants to believe that I can change, which I know I will be more healthy. Be more consistent, stay on top of things and make a routine of it is because I think she still loves me, but she's afraid of making a mistake for the kids and making a mistake of going back to the same cycle that has happened before, which I totally respect. Hanna is a fantastic mother. An incredible person, my best friend, the love of my life and I just wanted an opportunity to make this family whole again. But I can only control what I can control and I'm trying to continue to work on myself. Be here and show up every day and try to help show Hannah that I can be exactly what she needs and that our relationship is worth a shot.

It's hard. It's really hard. But nothing that's worthwhile is easy. I will never go back to not taking care of myself or being on top of my health. I'll never refuse to help, avoid work, or not believe I can do things. It led to letting Hanna down as a partner and husband. 

But I hope there is still love. I know we can fix things. I'm here and waiting for when Hanna wants to try. God I miss her. 

Thankful for these kids. And the purpose they give me everyday. ❤️

Came over as planned with Margo at 11:00 ish to allow Hannah to go to work and allow me some time with the kids. Hopefully going to be able to do bedtime tonight and dinner time with both. Asher, Marge's and Hannah, I talked to Hannah a little bit about how we could do the fair play plan that I will hold half the cars that I will ensure that no matter what I will be building and maintaining a healthy, balanced and equitable domestic home life and responsibilities as well as taken care of my mental health and ensuring that I am never the person that I was. I know that she's hurt. I know that she can't imagine taking the risk right now because she's worried that I will be that person again, but I never will be. I truly never will be. I am scared I will never be with my family. I'll never be around my kids all the time like I dreamed and hoped and planned. The part that I'm really trying to share with her is that we both don't want shared custody even though that's what would happen. We both are heartbroken. We both want healthy and safe homes for our kids and we both want to believe that there's hope I am fully on board to do the work. I'm ready to do all the hard work. I'm ready to learn. I'm ready to challenge myself and I'm ready to do a lot of things i was never ready to do like quit smoking weed like really making myself available in the evenings and going to bed at a reasonable time constantly and never ever giving up on my mental health or the routines that allow me to be my best. My family and my kids deserve my best and I really do believe that given that chance an opportunity, we will be such an amazing, loving and incredible family and I just hope that that chance will be given. But that said, I'm pretty aware that I need to kind of plan for the worst but hope for the best and that's really really hard. Even just saying, had I hate you look good, made her feel uncomfortable or it was inappropriate. So I'm trying my best to navigate this in a way that allows her to see that I hear her that I see her and that I want to be part of her life. I want to be her best friend and her lover and her husband. I will never let her down again. These kids will always have me. They will always have me at my best and I'm just wanting Hannah to be. Give me give me that chance if it was. If it's possible, I would truly truly love the opportunity to be part of this home again, but given she wants to have a separation agreement outlined next week and I need to maybe find a lawyer to really make sure I'm having someone look at that and advocate for me and try to understand how there is a possibility someday in the future months, weeks, whatever it is to be together again to be a family and to show her that I won't ever forget how I let her down and I will never let it happen again. Nothing means more to me than this family and that includes Hannah. I know a lot of people are separating the kids and Hanna but for me it's this is my family. It's all one units and it's very hard to imagine any element of us apart, even though that's what I am doing right now, living somewhere else. Anyway, just a little entry using the voice to write so this is a little bit different but maybe I'll start doing this more since it's actually a little bit easier.

 She does not see a path to loving me or being with me. Her only goal is to have a healthy co-parenting relationship. She is not setting a plan that lets me take care of my kids. It's always her that gets then each night and each morning. I just tag in when it's convenient for her. She's saying that it will be collaborative etc but she really hasn't made it that yet. At least to me. 

I asked again to set a plan. So I'm going to take both kids to the museum or something on Saturday. I guess by myself. I will have Margs when Hanna works today, Colleen (who won't even talk or look at me or come into the house) will be dropping off Asher off after SHE feeds him and picks him up. I'll get a bit of time before bed with him. That's it.

I am starting to get a bit frustrated with the lack of clarity or equality in access. But I also understand that's reflection of how things have been with her as the primary parent, but that was my fault I guess. But they'll never be that way again if I could just have the chance. 

I have asked her for a chance. To show her the changes she wants to see. She feels she's given enough. She won't respect herself if she comes back or wants to work on things. She says she'll still do the counseling for me but she's not there for the same reasons. Even the book she told me to read was about fixing things and now she's not wanting to really commit to fixing things so why am I reading this book about systems and how to communicate and fix things? 

So I'm trying to just be a co parent and focus on making plans for the kids and myself. How to involve myself with them everyday. She was hesitant when I asked about going to swimming lessons even. Like it's just so hard to understand.

She's only coming to the councilling to be a coparent. We're there for completely different reasons. I'm pretty damn devastated but enjoying time with Margs.

she keeps saying maybe in 6 months or down the line she could maybe see it but like she won't commit to a chance or working on things. She's done enough she says. Hard to see a path to what I want now.

I just keep thinking about her with someone else. My kids having a dad that isn't their dad when I'm not with them. I truly am so angry at myself.  She says she isn't interested in love or dating but who knows. I just want to work on this together and that dream is fading fast. I love her so much. 

But I'm doing all the right things for myself and for my kids. I'm willing to build systems and do things together. But it seems that's all not possible. Fuck.

The fact that I shared my concerns about us doing to much each time we added a kid doesn't mean anything now. Yet it meant me taking a leap of faith then. If I hadn't she said maybe it would affect our relationship. Like, I felt I had to to be with her.

The fact that she has never been clear about expectations for anythibg. The fact I always made time to check and ask about the days priorities and then I'd be told I did it wrong or did the wrong things. The fact that I always encouraged communication. 

I'm not saying that what I said or did or how I didn't put them first in the way I needed to didn't happen but this whole thing feels completely out of left field. I feel like she's giving up and breaking promises the same way I did. (Well differently)

Anyway..I'm just feeling really hurt and dealing with all the emotions that entails.

She is the love of my life and I'll do anything to be with her and my family. 

God this is hard.

About to start my first therapy with Norah since last year. And then weekly going forward.

I feel like the major points and I'll hopefully see if this aligns with Hannas feelings but:

- disconnect in our relationship with added responsibilities and 2nd kid. 
- my mental health causing fear, stress and worry that was completely unnecessary and unfair, and ultimately led to breaking Hannas trust. (She did say if I had just gone to the hospital than we would be fine, but I'm doing the work now, even more so... )
- shefault parent. I wasn't the partner or collaborator, planner and contributor that I should have been with our life. This may also connect to my mental wellbeing and a fear of failure. A fear of letting her and the kids down. Which is ultimately what happened. 
- communication, being heard and being able to be better communicators under stress and on the day to day. Making sure we feel heard. 
- the frustration of the lost time and lost selfs that we have had while we moved forward with life. 

I just hope that, in time, she will see that the things we added which are incredible blessings, our home, our kids, have also added pressure and stress to us both and it affected us in different ways. I know she doesn't believe people can change. That she doesn't know if she can love me. But the fact she WANTS to believe means a lot to me. It gives me hope that the love can be rebuild, the relationship rebuilt with fairness and strong communication, with a much more balance and fair split of day to days. I will never let my family down again.

Anyway. To therapy.

Been thinking about doing a book of photos for me and Hanna, for our lives together. To highlight the good. While we deal with the bad. Maybe.

I tried to say that counciling would help with that but she wanted to go after I've seen my doc on Tuesday for my first session. It was really hard but I'm trying to show through action that I'm committed to whatever this family needs. And for her space and recovery. But fuck that's hard. 
- I'm taking care of Margs at home today but going forward Hanna wants me to take care of them at a more neutral location.  Which that is really hard to hear too. I felt hope and I felt progress and now it feels like we're going backwards. My god I miss my family and love them so much. So going to see if I can take care of Margs at my parents place when I have time.
- still haven't seen Asher and it's eating me up. I've seen videos and talked to him on FaceTime to say goodnight and how much I love and miss him. But that's it. Hanna says well make plans for him to see me but it's hard to be apart. Really hard. I miss him and I worry so much about not being there for him as a family. I know we can fix this and show the kids how we fought for a healthier family and future. 
- trying to focus on a few basics, shower, teeth, walk, routines bedtime and wakeup. It's clear I let my health go, depression, ADHD, self esteem issues, all just really are at the root. I hate that it took this for me to really hear her. 
- listening and talking to Suzanne last night and one thing she said that is sticking with me is that it's really good for kids to see (even if they learn later in life) that their parents went through things and worked through it and put that effort to fix things, that it's really good for their own sense of problem solving and relationship ideation. 

God. I miss being part of a family. Being at home. Waking with them. Ups and downs. I'll never ever let this happen again. 

End of the day.. I'm really trying to give Hanna the space and time she needs, and hoping beyond hope that we can work this out for ourselves and for our kids. Every decision I'm making is about the kids first, my health and Hanna. I am so scared guys, but I'm keeping myself upright and doing things everyday. I'm feeling my feelings. Processing them. Also taking breaks and trying to relax and rest. It's gotta be a better balance.

One thing is clear, my kids and Hanna are the most important gift and I had the dream, and I didn't take care of myself the way I need to. Hanna is right. It took me a couple days but I'm really understanding where she's coming from and getting that I broke her trust, I haven't let her be herself and let her feel supported the way I promised and want her to feel. 

I hit 14k steps today. Didn't even take a walk. Just the house work, mopping, and I tried to start a couple projects - adding a whole wall of Ashers drawings and art beside his craft table in the dining room. Reorganized the arts stuff and craft so hopefully he likes that. 

During the day, however, Hanna and I actually HUNG OUT together with Margs. I made a simple lunch of like these... I guess, Italian sandwiches? Quite good anyway. I think? We talked and I think I let her feel heard. I tried anyway. It's tough for me to not try to fix everything and ask her to be home, I miss her and the kids so goddamn much. Having a couple hours with Margs was really amazing. I couldn't believe how much I missed her and how good it was to see her. It felt good that Hanna and I could do that. I am also giving her the space she requests. I hope we're building to be back in the same house soon.

And so Hanna shared how much easier it would be for the kids and her to have her home instead of me. I accepted that and it was really hard to think about doing it, but kids first, it's easy. So I texted a few people to see if I could stay elsewhere for a while. I'm hoping for just a couple days. But it's up to Hanna.

I'm now living at Lindsays MILs house. She's gone until Jan 31 so I've been pretty lucky to have it to myself. But it's not my house. I am pretty scared. Worried about losing my family and losing my life. Hanna and the kids. Everything. That's all my life is about. And I gotta show it, everyday.

Big wins today:

- talking to Hanna more often
- having Hanna and Margs over for lunch
- going to Margs potential daycare together to evaluate
- being trusted to have Margs at our home and Hanna trusting me to not overstep the space she needs

I hope these are good steps.

I had hoped there would be a visit today as Hanna said no problem yesterday but Asher is sick and it won't work today. I really miss them. I've asked if I can talk to them on the phone today. I'm thankful for these little updates and didn't know how much it meant to me to know where they are and what they are doing before. I'm so sad that ny inability to keep consistently on my mental health has led us to this place and I really do shoulder the blame for this break. I am holding onto hope that we can really figure this out. I know I can do my part.

G says it's just the way I am,.I have been beating myself up for 3+ decades and punishing myself. That really seems to hit. 

I think my biggest issue and what has really caused me to hesitate to take on more, to hesitate to take on work that feels boring, or that I don't know, is my self esteem and self confidence. I really don't think much of myself at all. 

I thought I'd be falling apart right now. I mean, I did for a day or two. Big emotional moments and things to process. I am so sad, and truly frustrated at myself. But, I'm trying to channel that into action, commitment and building better routines and making better decisions. I can't take care of others if I don't take care of myself. I haven't been the best husband or dad but I really know I can be. 

I have to rebuild my self esteem, maybe explore my parental history and whatever trauma? And we need to be in couples counciling so we can start hearing each other. I love her so much. I have to listen, and act right now. Listen and act. 

It is not about me. It's about my family. (Well it also is about investing in me, but I'm most determined and motivated to have Hanna and my kids in my arms again one day. That is my dream. I had my dream and now I have to work for it again. )

Never take things for granted. Ever.

memos.content:
Just had it out with Hanna. I don't understand. I asked for help from the grandparents. I guess to her she felt I was just taking over and trying to be the focus instead of Hanna. I didn't mean that nor want that. I was struggling with being happy. And my life. Feeling sad and alone in my own family. No hope of seeing myself in the mirror and liking what I see. 

She came home from work angry and while hot chocolate got spilt and Asher was upset she flashed me the most angry face. I asked Wat was up because I wanted to help and I had rushed down from my nap. She didn't call ahead to ask for help or let me know when she was coming. I guess I should have known but I was so tired. And I was clearly off because I hadn't taken my meds since my parents didn't come to help until 2pm and I know I needed sleep. 

I was devastated and things escalated. I wish I knew why. I wish I knew how to share how my head is and what's going on in it. I didn't want to take over or make Hanna feel anything less than loved and supported. I am so worried about her health. It's scary. I'm scared. I don't think she understands how scared I am. 

I ended up sharing, bluntly how I feel like I need help and maybe I'll just go check myself into the hospital at hsc and she said maybe it was a good idea. So I left and started driving. I shouldn't have left. I knew that as soon as I closed the door of the car but I didn't feel wanted at home at all. I didn't feel needed. It seems like I'm just good for doing productive things and my feelings, my dreams and my fears are not something to be discussed or shared. I turned around d and came home and by the time I was home Hanna told her mom I left her, and then her mom called my parents to say she thinks I need to go to hospital. I really don't. I need a supportive family. I need to feel loved for who I am. I need to be accepted for being whatever I am even if it's not a full equal in everything I am really trying. 

I come back and end up having Hannas mom wanting to talk to me on the phone. I tried to refuse. I didn't want to be lectured and I was quite pissed off she called my parents. (Side note, not even my parents called me to see how I was doing. Nothing.) She then starts to lecture me, and tell me I need to go to hospital and that she's talked to my parents and believes the same. I'm beyond insulted. I am the most active and loud advocate for mental health and have done more for myself and grown more as a man and person than anyone including Colleen. I held my tongue and tried to share how disappointed I was with her and how I don't need help and she's not listening to me, just like Hanna wasn't and my parents never have. 

End up saying I'm done and passed it back to Hanna. We continued into it. I just needed someone to fucking care about me. To say things will be ok. I have kept all my shit to myself for several days and focused everything on helping Hanna and the family. Yet it's still not enough. She made references constantly to equal but I'm not equally capable. We made a promise to each other to be supportive and patient with this kid adventure and she is always the one to break that. Always the one to attack my effort or results. I never ever ever criticize her or anything like that, her efforts at the home and at work and with family is unquestioned. I know shes in so much pain and I'm so scared and it's affecting me too. I don't sleep. If I do it's for like 15min then nightmares wake me. 

I just feel so lost and alone in my own house and it feels like no matter how hard I work for the family and how much I sacrifice and try to do more and more and more, it's never enough. More is always needed. I can never start to be comfortable and feel good about my efforts. And it sucks. I never said I would be able to match Hannas work ethic or drive or ability. I never claimed to do that and I was open that I struggle and need more downtime, more sleep, and more support. That was clear from the beginning of our dating to now and it's really starting to be clear that I'll never ever be the man she wanted. I am honestly so depressed and now that Colleen and my parents are both informed that I'm a fucking unhealthy unbalanced idiot, which isn't true at all, I have no idea how to handle the days or hours ahead. I am so sad. So fucking sad. 

But hey..Hannas getting her rest so that's good. I just have to get used to the fact that I'm not going to feel loved or supported or seen or respected in the way I expected when we got married. That sucks. And I'm not gonna be able to sleep tonight unless I get baked enough I guess. 

Left all the family group chats. Not gonna say anything to anyone about how I'm feeling or doing anymore. It seems that as much as people told me they would be here to listen and help they really didn't mean it. Just like my friends. I have to stop trusting people. 

I sent Colleen some texts to try to explain and also apologize that things have been confused. She doesn't seem to have the whole story..but her comments on the phone made it very clear she doesn't see me as irreplaceable either. I am disposable. Who cares about me. If I'm struggling when Hanna is struggling I deserve to be lectured about how I'm treating "her daughter". Ownership. She made it clear Hanna can be taken I guess. That sucks. 

I tried to apologize for leaving to go to the hospital but that didn't matter either. So I'm just sat downstairs..I took all my bedding and pillows down here too. Hanna said she didn't want me near her. I'm literally getting shit on for trying to focus on everyone and ensure I'm also well enough to shoulder more of the load while Hanna deals with this health situation. Which is the # 1 priority for me. I don't see how nobody sees that.

I am saying I don't see a point in continuing life but I would never take myself away from my kids. I just feel so depressed and alone in my own family. My own house. I don't have a safe place anymore. I am truly alone.

# A Good Talk Wednesday and a Busy Tuesday

Tuesday was wildly busy. Work has been busy for me at the government with April (my manager) still away on stress leave, though she is coming back today which is great news. I'm taking a moment to try a proper entry using my newly setup 'memos' software, which I've self-hosted on the opti-scoot. It's kind of empowering being able to to not only use these neat pieces of software, but also be able to self-host it and own my data. Who knows what the future brings with all the AI and cloud stuff, some good, some bad - but I'd prefer SOME of my data not be available to them. 

Anyway, Tuesday. A quick morning to get the kids out the door, and also catching up on tasks at work, as well as in my new 'Todoist' approach. It's quite nice actually, I can just dump all my tasks, projects, thoughts, reminders into one place and organize them later. Syncs up with GCalendar, and has a desktop application which I like. Got a few things done for the home lab, spun up a network-mapping service called homelable which will take some time to work on. I'm **very** behind on my documentation, it's just a pile of random, disorganized notes in Obsidian right now, but eventually I'll be moving it into a nicely organized BookStack instance (again, self hosted). These things are bringing me a lot of joy. And, the restoration of the Plex library continues, we're at about ~10TB of the original 24TB that was there before the troubles. 

Tuesday evening after work was cool though. Asher got to go play on the ice at the MTS Centre during the 1st intermission of the Moose game. Bunch of family came, my parents, sister, nephew and Hanna's family, which really showed a lot of love for Asher. He was so excited to be there - and you could tell he was beaming before and after being on the ice. A whole wack of free timbits didn't hurt either. I took as much video and photos as I could, with Margaux trying to escape and jump on me, but I think they turned out okay. What a great way to end his first hockey season, a really special moment. When we left about 10 min into the 2nd period, as it was a weekday evening after all, he was **very** upset but we got through it and got the kids to bed. Both Hanna and I crashed pretty early. Only thing that was really challenging was that Colleen seemingly had an absolute breakdown at entry with Margaux and Chad, as she couldn't figure out (or didn't know how to) the TicketMaster/Jets app. She apparently had a meltdown, and honestly, I just find it so frustrating to see her do things I used to do, that she called me out on and encouraged Hanna to make an issue in our relationship. It's very hypocritical, and that always makes me less empathetic than I should be. Poor Margaux saw Hanna trying to help from inside, but since the entry has a large gap between entry/scanning tickets, and where you get checked for security, she couldn't really help directly and poor Margaux was freaking out. Apparently my parents saw this, and honestly - it just shocks me that Colleen has so little ability to be honest and just say "i need help with this". She tells people shes incredible at technology, but she really isn't. Then, to top it off, Colleen and Chad left straight after the 1st intermission, when Hanna was visiting with my parents who were in another section. Kind of rude, kind of wildly rude. But, overall - a great night for Asher, Margaux and the family. 

Today has been a bit hectic to start, as I didn't get time to make the lunches for the kids last night. Got up after another night of Margaux crawling into our bed to sleep, constantly poking and scratching at my skin which makes for a bit of a restless night, but alas, as long as shes comfortable. She did have to recover from that trauma yesterday. Made lunches as soon as we woke, got the kids bags ready, and then went back to bed after they left for about 45min to let my Concerta kick it. I always find the day starts better when I get a chance to rest/nap after I take my Concerta, and I pop back up and get at it.

Work was busy, but April is back and catching up so that's really encouraging. I had to get back on my horse as the last couple weeks I've been on cruise a bit, doing things as they are needed, but mostly at the last minute. Been spending a lot of time to get the opti-scoot and scootNAS back up, the Plex server back up and going after the end of my old machine. Spent my day working on the new manitoba.ca Drupal translations, and had a couple meetings to attend. I also had a personal therapy session with Norah at lunch, which was my first therapy session in probably 6 or 7 months. Things were going well, so we suggested a larger gap between appointments, plus I had run out of coverage so no need to spend the $125/hr if its not really needed. 

The therapy session was solid, caught up, talking a bit about Hanna and I's discussion on parenting styles, the trips we've taken, the kids, work... overall, again, things are going really well. The difference between me 2-3 years ago and now is night and day, and I couldn't be more proud of myself for really being a more healthy person mentally than I have ever been in my life. Especially since I have my wife and my kids to look after. 

After the meetings, Hanna and I spoke for a bit about the session and continued our conversation about the parenting styles/co-parenting stuff she brought up. I reiterated, I'm open to doing couples therapy, but that I didn't quite understand what would change from my end, as I'm already open, willing and taking accountability for mistakes when they are made. I'm going to try to be a bit more present and interactive with the kids, and less "just in the room", when possible, so that should help. We also agree that what she wants from a co-parent is someone who would listen, adjust and prioritize her priorities, which I do, but that quite often she doesn't present those priorities to me cleanly or allow me to ask questions without getting defensive. I think it was a good conversation, ended with a hug and seemingly made her feel more on the same page, which is great. I do feel things are going incredible well, especially with how much outside stress (world, geopolitics, finance) we have going on day to day. 

Going to end this here - and note that I'm working with Claude Code to develop an importer so I can bring in my Daylio journal entries into this new memos system, as I think I'd like to use this for the future. Would be cool if my kids could read it one day, even if there may be some TMI in it.

# Bleh and Beyond
> originally created in Day One

#journal #relationships #family #mood-meh 

- Discussed couples therapy with Hanna about parenting styles.
- 🚼 Daughter curled up with me in bed.
- 💻 Submitted first pull request on GitHub.
- 📋 Transitioning to Todoist for task management.
- 😔 Feeling down about interrupted sleep with Hanna.

Winding down in bed tonight after a day that felt both full and a little heavy. Late this afternoon, Hanna brought up the idea of couples therapy—she said she loves me and is happy with our life, but wants to open up some communication about our parenting styles. We both get frustrated with the kids sometimes, and she suggested I be more patient. It caught me off guard. The conversation came after her therapy session, when she initially thought her therapist might do couples work with us, but ended up clarifying that wouldn't be a good idea—which was actually a relief, since I felt uncomfortable about that.

All this landed harder because back in January 2024, Hanna left and took the kids, which completely shocked me. We did work things out, but it took me quitting weed, getting healthier, and making a lot of changes. Since then, things have genuinely been good. Still, it feels like she’s always looking for areas to improve, which is fine, but sometimes it feels unnecessarily negative. When she brought up therapy, we talked through it. I said I'd be open, but really wanted to know what outcome she was looking for. We both agreed that when she communicates a need, I always try to address it, so I don’t really know what would change after couples therapy. She wants our parenting styles to be more aligned, and feels she carries more of the mental load—I don’t agree, but I do think we work well as a team. As I was journaling, my two-year-old daughter came to curl up with me in bed, while Hanna was already in Asher’s room because he’d woken up. We almost never get to sleep together all night, and that’s tough.

The therapy talk was definitely the hardest part of the day, but there were grounding moments too. I spent time at my computer, SSHing into my servers and working on deploying some self-hosted software and services for my home lab. I’ve been switching to Todoist to organize my endless stream of tasks and ideas, which has been helpful with my ADHD and GAD. Today was also my last day off of a four-day weekend; hoping for more focus and productivity at work tomorrow.

A highlight was submitting my first pull request on GitHub for a repo that isn’t mine—a custom widget for Dynacat, a customizable dashboard. Adding issues, testing, and submitting a PR made me feel accomplished. I’m also building my own documentation wiki in BookStack, and using Gemini Pro and Claude for project support and coding help. Haven’t gamed much lately, which is odd, but I guess when my ADHD brain is firing on all cylinders, there’s not much room to relax. Even now, past midnight, I’m still wired despite being up since 7am.

What I want to remember most from today is successfully contributing to a GitHub project—feeling like I can do so much, even if my constant ideation sometimes overwhelms me. Dumping tasks into Todoist helps keep the chaos somewhat managed.

Right now, I’m feeling a bit down about never getting a full night’s sleep with Hanna—always interrupted by the kids—and my brain is still racing, probably because my Concerta has worn off. I might play SteamDeck in bed to wind down, but honestly, I just feel sad. Or maybe tired and too wired to sleep. Despite Hanna’s reassurance, her therapy suggestion still feels like a failure on my part.

If I had to sum up today in one word, it would be: bleh.

Overall, today was a lot—emotionally and mentally full, with some wins and some heaviness, but I made it through.
